title: mpv's tct video output makes nvim segfault

labels.name: bug-crash
labels.description: issue reporting a crash or segfault

body:
<!-- Before reporting: search existing issues and check the FAQ. -->
Yes, you read that right. I tried to play a video file in a `:terminal` buffer using mpv. Why, you ask? I found it in the man page, wanted to try it out as a joke and happened to have a nvim session with a terminal buffer open at the time. Pure coincidence paired with curiosity.

Let me preface this that I have no need to actually see this working. I just felt that, even for abnormal circumstances, it should not be possible to predictably and reliably induce a segfault in a non-alpha/beta/rc/whatever version. Feel free to ignore if you think it's okay to crash for a nonsensical use case like this, I honestly can't bring myself to disagree.


- `nvim --version`:
```                                           
NVIM v0.4.3
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.0.5
Compilation: /usr/bin/cc -march=x86-64 -mtune=generic -O2 -pipe -fno-plt -O2 -DNDEBUG -DMIN_LOG_LEVEL=3 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wno-unused-parameter -Wstrict-prototypes -std=gnu99 -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wmissing-prototypes -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Wvla -fstack-protector-strong -fdiagnostics-color=always -DINCLUDE_GENERATED_DECLARATIONS -D_GNU_SOURCE -DNVIM_MSGPACK_HAS_FLOAT32 -DNVIM_UNIBI_HAS_VAR_FROM -I/build/neovim/src/build/config -I/build/neovim/src/neovim-0.4.3/src -I/usr/include -I/build/neovim/src/build/src/nvim/auto -I/build/neovim/src/build/include
Compiled by builduser

Features: +acl +iconv +tui
See ":help feature-compile"

   system vimrc file: "$VIM/sysinit.vim"
  fall-back for $VIM: "/usr/share/nvim"

Run :checkhealth for more info
```
- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: ) behaves differently? Does not apply, since `:terminal` is a Neovim-only feature.
- Operating system/version: Arch Linux, current (at time of writing)
- Terminal name/version: Kitty 0.17.4
- `$TERM`: `xterm-kitty`

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`

```
nvim -u NORC
# Alternative for shell-related problems:
# env -i TERM=ansi-256color "$(which nvim)"
:terminal mpv --vo=tct 'some/video/file/here.mp4'
```

### Actual behaviour

Nvim segfaults shortly after playback starts, corrupting the terminal session. How long it takes to segfault depends on the video file, and it actually survives some extremely short files, but most do crash it.

From what I've seen in my limited testing, the time-to-crash depends solely on the video file. I tried using multiple different terminal emulators for nvim itself, and while none of them would complain about mpv if run directly from the shell, nvim would always crash at the same location in the video.

If you want a file to repro, I could provide one.

### Expected behaviour

Nvim should not segfault.
